ARTICULUS SECUNDUS.
De gravitate & Levitate.
1. TRes præcipuæ sunt Philosophorum sententiæ de Gravitate & Levi-

l.i: tate: Prima est Peripateticorum, secunda Epicureorum, tertia quor-

main_text.l: 2. Peripatetici statuunt primò, duas esse qualitates motrices elemento-
rum & aliorum corporum, scilicet gravitas & levitas, & utraque vel est
talis simpliciter, vel secundum quid. Grave in genere dicitur illud quod

l.i: tendit deorsum; leve vero quod tendit sursum. Grave simpliciter dicitur il-
lud quod substat omnibus ut terra: Grave vero secundum quid est illud
quod ita substat aliquibus, ut tamen quibusdam aliis superemineat, ut a-
qua, quae igne & aere est inferior, terrâ vero est superior. Leve simpliciter
dicitur illud quod superemineat omnibus, ut ignis: Leve vero secundum
quid est quod ita superemineat aliquibus, ut tamen alteri subsit, ut aër qui
terrâ & aquâ est superior, igne vero inferior. Quare Levitas communiter
definitur potentia naturalis quâ subjectum movetur sursum. Gravitas vero de-

main_text.l: finitur potentia naturalis quâ subjectum movetur deorsum. Et utraque vel est
talis simpliciter, vel secundum quid.

page.notes: Heading: the printed "ARTICVLVS SECVNDVS." and "SECVNDA PARS" are transcribed with u for the vowel and v for the consonant as the rules require. The large initial T of paragraph 1 is joined to "Res" as "TRes". The line after paragraph 1 has a flourish that reads "Recentiorum..." in the scan; it is transcribed as "Recentiorum." without the ellipsis. Italic type in paragraphs 2–4 is inferred from the scan and may be partly wrong; the boundaries of the italic runs in paragraph 2 are uncertain. Uncertain letters: "Caeterum" (ae/æ) and "tantum"/"tantùm" accent; "aere"/"aëre" as printed. "quæstio," at the right below the last line is treated as the catchword and is not repeated in the text. Print spelling "putum"/"putus" and "aquae" are left as printed. No margin notes, no footnotes, no reference marks.
